title: sell() keeps a second value override beside `cost`: the `sell_value` prop replaces sale_price(it) after it is computed (gear.py:168). Fold it into the item valuation, e.g. a `sale_price` hook on Item that honours `sell_value` and otherwise halves listed_cost(), so selling has one value mechanism. Also the sale_price docstring says trade goods keep full value, but the function always halves.

history.summary: Selling now has one value mechanism. I added `Item.sale_price()` in `dungdra/items.py`: if the item has a `sell_value` prop, that is the price of one unit; otherwise it is half of `listed_cost()`, rounded down, and an unpriced item is refused. `gear.sell()` now just calls `it.sale_price() * qty`, so the override that ran after the price was computed is gone. I removed the old module-level `sale_price()` function and its docstring, which wrongly said trade goods keep full value. In `tests/unit/test_items.py` the existing tests now call the new method, and one new test checks that `sell_value` replaces the half price, even on an item with no listed cost. Unit tests, the full test suite (599 passed), ruff and dev-gate all pass. The ticket names no acceptance tests, so there was nothing to run with `--runxfail`. One thing I left alone: `sell()`'s log message still says "(half price)", even when `sell_value` sets a different price.
